'''''Cotoneaster cochleatus''''', the '''Yunnan cotoneaster''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Rosaceae]].<ref name="CTTCC" >{{cite web |url=https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/CTTCC |title=''Cotoneaster cochleatus'' (CTTCC) |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2022 |website=EPPO Global Database |publisher=European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization |access-date=14 June 2022 |quote=Cultivated as an ornamental and naturalized at least in Britain }}</ref><ref name="RHS_97974" >{{cite web |title=''Cotoneaster cochleatus'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/97974/i-cotoneaster-cochleatus-i/details |date=2022 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=14 June 2022 |quote=Synonyms; ''Cotoneaster microphyllus'' var. ''cochleatus'' (Franch.) Rehder & E.H. Wilson ''Cotoneaster melanotrichus'' misapplied ... 4 suppliers }}</ref> It is native to rocky slopes in [[Tibet]], [[Sichuan]], and [[Yunnan]] in China, and it has been introduced to the United Kingdom, Belgium and New York State.<ref name="722448-1" >{{cite POWO |id=722448-1 |title=''Cotoneaster cochleatus'' (Franch.) G.Klotz |access-date=13 June 2022 }}</ref> Its [[specific epithet]] ''cochleatus'' refers to its twisting stem.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gledhill |first1=David |date=2008 |title=The Names of Plants |edition=Fourth |location=Cambridge; New York |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=113 |isbn=9780521685535 }}</ref>

A drought-tolerant creeping shrub reaching {{cvt|1|ft|m|1}} tall but spreading to {{cvt|6|ft|m|0}}, and hardy in [[Hardiness zone|USDA zones]] 5 through 7, it is considered a valuable landscaping plant by the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]].<ref name="MBG_286628" >{{cite web |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286502 |title=''Cotoneaster cochleatus'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Plant Finder |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=14 June 2022 }}</ref> The [[Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International]] lists it in its [[Invasive Species Compendium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/113508 |title=Datasheet ''Cotoneaster cochleatus'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2022 |website=Invasive Species Compendium |publisher=CAB International |access-date=14 June 2022 }}</ref> With its small glossy leaves, tiny rose-like flowers, showy red fruit, and low growth habit, it has found use in [[bonsai]].<ref name="MBG_286628" />
